description:
Located in one of Asheville's oldest historic districts, walkable to UNC-Asheville, the Omni Grove Park Inn, restaurants, wine shops, markets, greenways, parks and more! Downtown is walkable on well-lit sidewalks (under 2 miles), a 5-min drive away.

The newly-installed UBIQUITI access point is your reliable connection for online meetings and networking.

neighborhood_overview: Our beautiful Grove Park Historic District close to downtown is a safe, friendly neighborhood with well-lit sidewalks, wonderful gardens, parks, and a fantastic greenway linking to the center of Asheville.
host_about:
Welcome to Terrace Cottage!

For fifteen years we have enjoyed hosting visitors in our Asheville, North Carolina cottage from across the country and around the world including England and Ireland, Greece, Canada, Mexico and Cuba, Argentina, Japan and The Phillipines. We welcome guests from around the corner, across the US and our international visitors as well! Our college-age daughter grew up listening to many different languages in the driveway.

We enjoy traveling including work-and-play trips to Ireland, England, Sweden and Greece. Twenty years here at our residence built in 1926 and our adjacent Terrace Cottage was built in 2000.

We love working in our perennial beds and veggie gardens.

I'm an online entrepreneur designing and marketing wooden playthings for young people. I also collect and blog about vintage wooden toys.

My wife is a clinician with UNC-Chapel Hill School of Medicine. 

We love living in Asheville and are always happy to return home when away. It is a nationally-celebrated and uniquely beautiful mountain city overflowing with eclectic opportunities for enjoying first-rate dining, entertainment, crafts and artwork. The Blue Ridge Parkway entrance is ten minutes from our home, leading to the North Carolina Arboretum, Mount Pisgah, Craggy Gardens, and Mount Mitchell- the highest elevation east of the Rocky Mountains. 

I fly fish and welcome inquiries regarding our local waters. My favorite streams are under an hour away and have been rated in Trout Unlimited's Top 100. There are excellent fly shops and outfitters nearby if you need them.

Walking, running and cycling are huge in Asheville and there are too many options to mention from neighborhood greenways and hill climbs to maniacal day-longs as well, contact us for info. Our local runner's and cyclist's shops are just blocks away.

Speaking of walkable- ditto our supermarket and specialty/whole foods markets, cafes, coffee shops, local theater, pharmacies, UNC-Asheville, botanical gardens, awesome kid's parks and more.

Thanks for looking at Terrace Cottage and we welcome your inquiries!

neighborhood_overview: My neighborhood is a working class neighborhood that is about as close to downtown as you can be without being in the mix of it. It is a few minutes walk to almost anything you would want, yet a complete neighborhood feel. My neighbors are all friendly we are diverse in our socio-economic, racial, political, age & gender make-ups.
host_about:
I like to have fun & meet new people and hear about new experiences so as to expand my own understanding of this life.
I like to do fun building projects and see how I might take old materials and recreate them in a new fashion.
I am fairly laid back and I prefer to host people who are also laid back and appreciate bohemian lifestyles. 
I appreciate the urban and rural ways of life and try to live them both to the fullest.
I like new experiences so I've had a variety of jobs/careers: I've been a dishwasher; a farmer; a whitewater rafting guide, a wildland fire manager (in over half the country and other countries too); I served as Director of the Environmental Center @ the local University; got with some awesome colleagues and co-founded the Asheville Buncombe Food Policy Council, I proudly serve as a Guardian ad Litem (child advocacy in the court system) and I do a little community organizing around economic, environmental & overall social justice.

As far as how my style relates to you, my neighbor, I am real hands off! I have a full life and don't hang around too much....but when I do, I like to relax, converse and giggle.

Lots of great live music, delicious restaurants, local festivals, amazing art scene, and a happening dance community.  Oh yeah, a healing arts mecca.  Plenty of yoga and therapeutic options around these parts.
I'll tell you where to find the best huevo rancheros you've ever had in your life!

Our neighborhood is known as "South French Broad" (named after the river that flows through town) and is ideally situated in Asheville. You can be at the Biltmore, many of the South Slope breweries or downtown restaurants or right in the middle of all the galleries of the River Arts District all in less than five minutes drive. neighborhood_overview:

My grandparents bought the three acres in 1945 because a double rainbow hung over the eastern view. 10 Cherry Lane was where they lived until my family moved in with them. Four kids and two parents living in the upstairs at 10 had my grandparents moving quickly to build their dream house. 12 was designed by a protege of Frank Lloyd Wright and is a one-of-a-kind style with plenty of light and outside areas for calm meditative moments or kickball. host_about:
My grandparents built this house in 1959. My grandfather was a Major General, head of the 13th AD, and a graduate of West Point in 1915, along with Eisenhower and Omar Bradley. After getting shot in WW2, his military career ended and he and my grandmother moved to Asheville so he could run the VA Hospital in Oteen. 

The house next door and three acres is what they bought in 1945 after witnessing a double rainbow over the mountains. After my mother and father moved us four kids to the upstairs of that house, my grandparents got an architect who studied with Frank Lloyd Wright to design the mid-century modern house next door, and my childhood was spent going between the houses. 

Four years ago I came up to renovate the place in order to sell it, but after watching a full moon rise over the mountains, I fell in love with it all over again and bought it. It's a comfort knowing this property has never left our family. I can feel all my relations here and enjoy the memories I had, mostly with my loving, brilliant, funny grandmother in this house. It has been a gathering spot for many famous people, including Ike and Mamie, who were close friends of my grandparents, and Carl Sandburg. 

I am an artistic welder and a singer and have travelled all over the world entertaining the troops for the Dept of Defense. Along the path of my travels, I always appreciated the kindness of locals who guided me when lost or recommended flavorful local places set apart from the tourist track. I'm here to offer you the same guidance.

There are sculptures and furniture inside and around my property that I made. 

 I love meeting new people, and I also love my privacy. I respect guests privacy as well and am available with any questions, concerns, interests you may have, but otherwise will not intrude. I live upstairs, and I am sensitive to being quiet. I encourage my guests to feel right at home. 

The expansive yard has plenty of areas to sit and enjoy a cup of coffee or a cocktail. The garden beds have herbs you are welcome to use.

Feel free to text with any questions prior to your stay as well as during your stay. My goal is for everyone who books the studio to enjoy the view, the birds, the wildlife, and the close proximity to everything fun while feeling far away, so much so, that they want to come back!!!

neighborhood_overview:

Our property is one of six houses that surrounds a one acre park where you will regularly find families practicing baseball and soccer and neighbors running with their dogs amidst the towering oak trees that give the neighborhood its name. Our home was previously owned by a large loving family who ran a greenhouse on the adjacent property which now houses a family owned Hispanic Market. A distinctive feature of our home is the Christmas tree planted by the former family in the front yard over 40 years ago that now towers over the house. We fully remodeled and lovingly restored the interior of our home in 2003, including building the apartment in the former carriage "house" space. host_about: Transplants from Southern California in 1992 we have loved raising our family in the Asheville area. Our eldest, a daughter, was married in 2015 and lives with her husband (who works for Sierra Nevada) and our grandson in the Hendersonville area. Our middle son lives and works in downtown Asheville and our youngest son is a 2020 graduate from our small private school and is headed to college in the fall. Tim is a licensed general contractor and insurance adjuster. Elisa is an artist and art teacher at a PK-12 private school. We have restored multiple historic properties in the Asheville area over the last 24 years including a condemned house in the Montford Historic District for which Tim won the prestigious Griffin Award for historic preservation in 2004. Our commitment to faithful restoration is apparent in this property which we fully remodeled and restored in 2003. We have been landlords for several long term rentals in the area for 29 years, including this apartment, and have enjoyed the transition to vacation rental. We love both stimulating and laid back conversation with our friends and appropriate mood music (we can't live without our Bose Sounddock or Sonos), good food (esp Mexican) and craft beer and wine. Our love of the outdoors takes us to California's Yosemite National Park for camping every summer and to our family condo on the gulf coast as often as we can get there. We enjoy hiking and biking and late night fire pits. We can point you to the usual and the unusual spots in Asheville so just ask. We can make a church recommendation if that's important to you. We think we have the best friends in the world and we especially love making new ones. We look forward to your visit!

host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

Your private, spacious bungalow is located just a 10-minute walk to downtown Asheville and everything downtown has to offer. This two room suite has a lovely sitting area, dining table, Queen sized bed and Jacuzzi tub.

This bungalow is part of the adjacent Chestnut Street Inn and has received a 100% Sanitation Rating from the Department of Health & Human Services of Asheville.
neighborhood_overview:
Enjoy the convenience of the Chestnut Hill Historical District of Asheville. Stroll a quick 10 minutes to downtown for restaurants, cafes, shops and everything else this quaint town offers.

There are several restaurants and cafes that are within a 5-minute walk as well. We love Liberty House for amazing breakfast and lunch and great coffee drinks, Elements for organic fresh juice and salads, Plant for exquisite vegan fare, City Bakery for a casual lunch and delicious baked goods to name a few.
host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

description:
Our guests keep telling us, "you're super close to everything we want to see in Asheville": Downtown, Biltmore Estate, Blue Ridge Parkway, the River Arts District, hiking, biking, water sports. This cozy, private studio apartment, is UPSTAIRS in a 2013-built home, with private entrance; comfy queen bed, bath, sitting/TV room and kitchenette. Continental breakfast included. ALL are welcome. See below the special precautions we're taking due to Covid-19.

The space
- Because of the Covid-19 pandemic, we follow Airbnb protocols to prevent spread of the virus: In addition to using freshly laundered sheets & towels, we switch bed spread and shams between guests, wipe down every touchable surface with commercial anti-bacterial cleanser, wash all dishes & utensils, provide commercially pre-packaged portions for your continental breakfast, wear masks during your check-in or use a self-check-in. If you have questions, don't hesitate to ask. Now for the description
neighborhood_overview:
We built our home in the Kenilworth neighborhood in part because it is convenient to everything in Asheville. We are a 5-minute drive to our delightful downtown, to Biltmore Estate, to tons of restaurants, breweries, shops and the mall on Tunnel Road; and a 10-minute drive to the River Arts District or to the Blue Ridge Parkway. We are also an easy drive to dozens of hiking trails.
If you’re up for a little walk in the neighborhood, within 5-minutes of our home you’ll see even more spectacular views of the mountains toward Mt. Pisgah to the west, and a panoramic view over downtown Asheville.
You might even see bears and wild turkeys. But remember they’re not tame!
host_about:
Michael and I moved to Asheville in late 2011 and built our arts and crafts cottage in 2013.  I grew up in New Orleans and we enjoy getting back to the “Big Easy” as often as possible.  You’ll see flavors of New Orleans around our home.  My work as a licensed esthetician has taken me to Atlanta, St. Lucia and Saint Simons Island, GA as well as New Orleans.  

Michael grew up in the Atlanta area and has lived and worked around the world.  After spending 3 1/2 years in western Ethiopia, he lived in Indonesia for 7 years, then Indianapolis for about 15 years.    

Michael’s work in international nonprofits has allowed us to travel together in Asia, Africa and South America. You’ll see hints of those travels in our home.  Since my father was born in Sicily, we have enjoyed reconnecting with family back in the “old country.”

I am a bit of a cinemaphile.  In addition to my collection of old movies (even some old video cassettes - - and yes we still have a VCR in addition to our DVD player), I enjoy the oldies and classics on TV and Netflix.  I also enjoy cooking - - occasionally resorting to some of my old "N’awlins" dishes.

We enjoy gardening.  I specialize on the designing and Michael handles a lot of the physical work - - at least outside.  I love creating and tending miniature gardens that enjoy the year-round beauty of our sunroom.

Since Michael recently retired, we’re doing some extra travel.  And my years of dancing on stage and theatre just wouldn't let me go, so I continue to enjoy tap and modern dance.

host_about:
My name is Shauna. I have lived in the Asheville area since 2009. I met my husband here and we have been married since 2012. We have 2 children. A 5 year old girl and a 1 year old boy.  

After our first child was born I became a "work from home" mom, and now I oversee our rentals. We started our first rental in December of 2016 and I absolutely fell in love with doing it, so much so, that we started up another rental in March of 2018. I can't put my finger on what exactly I love about it, but I just do. I love the freedom it gives me to be with my kids and handle the "unexpected." I also love that it allows me to be more hands on with guests or handle issues or needs in person vs. over the phone or having someone else do it for me. 

5 things I can't live without.....
coffee
massages
doing anything and everything outdoors
giving my kids kisses and hugs everyday and playing with them
and, yeah....wine and beer

My husband and I are very laid back, fun, outdoorsy people. We love everything outdoors. You name it, we do it. We also love to travel, especial out of the country.
Favorite hobbies include gardening, canning, raising cows, fishing, mountain biking, hiking, and exploring new restaurants.

We are always on the go and it seems like something unexpected always happens or changes our plans, so I would have to say our life motto is, "just roll with the punches and deal with it as best you can." Nothing is perfect and stuff happens. How you handle it determines the end result.

host_about:

I have lived in many places and have had the privilege of some amazing  travel experiences internationally -  off the gringo path in Peru, living above an artist's gallery in Indonesia, going to school in the Loire Valley in France,  hiking into an active volcano in Nicaragua . . . the privilege was not about the places I stayed, but in the people I encountered who helped ignite my soul in some way or uncover what living is truly about. All of my travels and experiences have brought me back to this mystical and magical mountainous wonderland. And now I wish to share it with you!

host_about:
Early exposure to the Blue Ridge Mountains and a love of cycling initially drew me to Asheville. The artistic diversity of the community reawakened my interest in architecture and fed a desire to contribute to Asheville's thriving downtown. 
	
Built in 1924, 59 Broadway came on the market in 2013 and was unusual in that it had only served as warehouse space with consequently very little infrastructure, thus providing a clean canvas for my modernist vision. Having sat empty for a decade, it was in remarkably great shape. But most importantly, it had SOUL.

After a year of planning, a project incorporating the interplay of natural, urban, and personal environments with attention to space, lighting, quality, and simplicity was begun. Twelve-foot ceilings, original hardwood flooring, simple layout, and uncluttered space help imbue the feeling of warmth and calm that initially drew me in. Unlike any other historic building downtown, it’s newly engineered windows all along the northern wall provide an abundance of natural light further enhancing the unique ambiance.

My wife Constance and I, along with the seasoned guidance of an interior designer, picked furnishings that we would want in our own home, including art and ceramics throughout made by local artists who are also our friends. We especially love the bird’s eye view of the city’s comings and goings while perched on the full length window seats. Mesmerizing.

We hope you agree that the integrated sound system rocks and that the splurge mattresses feel heavenly after a day of exploring all that this vibrant city and surroundings has to offer.

host_about:
I love to travel and soak up as much local culture as I can wherever I go, so I decided to share my home with people like you that share this passion. 
  I grew up in Atlanta and discovered Asheville by way of Maui. I  lived on Maui and Kauai for a few years and when it came time to move back closer to family a Maui  friend suggested Asheville as an alternative to the big city.  He’d grown up in Chapel Hill and in Asheville. 
 So, after enough culture shock back in Atlanta I decided to explore Asheville in the late 90’s. After being here for a week or so wuth my Boxer Buddy I knew I'd found our new home.  I'd also developed a love of old houses growing up in Atlanta so bought this 1927 bungalow from a friend in 2000. 
 In 2006 I decided to create a new space with a view. Only by cleaning my gutters did I notice what a great view to the west there was from a slightly higher perspective. host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

They say that wherever you go, there you are.

We say, when you go to Asheville, this is where you want to be. Right here, in the heart of Asheville. Right here, on N. Lexington Ave., in a building once home to farmers and growers and today the heart of all things trendy, artsy and quintessential.

Because here, in 566 square-feet of industrial loft space, exposed brick, pops of color, and layered textures, Unit 202 offers an only-in-Asheville kind of retreat: handpicked décor and vintage furnishings, curated artwork and upholstered barn doors.

A home-away-from-home that is both on trend and yet, thoroughly welcoming.
neighborhood_overview:
☀☀☀ LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION! ☀☀☀
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of N. Lexington Avenue.

This is the most hip and quintessential street in Asheville – a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. This is a place where high-end art galleries abut record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

80 LEX is your no-compromise-required destination: both urban and urbane, situated right in the beating heart of our vibrant city. Enveloped by the energy and excitement of downtown life, Unit 202 embodies and embraces the Asheville scene – a scene that draws designers and artists, creatives and music lovers, foodies and artisanal beverage aficionados a
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

description: Embrace the unique charm of this boutique space in an iconic red brick property. The loft-inspired private apartment features exposed original walls, dark surfaces, contrasting textures and patterns, an array of unique furnishings, and curated artwork throughout.
neighborhood_overview: The property sits on a quintessential street in Asheville – a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs; just a door. This is a place where high-end art galleries abut record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

I am a certified yoga teacher and love sharing the benefits of the practice with others. Yoga is one of the tools I use in my effort to maintain a healthy lifestyle that incorporates among other things a plant based diet, herbs, regular cleansing and detoxification.  

As an artist and graphic designer, my vision is to communicate respect for our planet, and to recognize the urgency to reconnect harmoniously with nature, through the creation of everyday objects and mandalas with recycled materials.

Look for your dream home. Hike to your heart's content. Just two blocks to vibrant West Asheville's eclectic and popular eateries, breweries, performance halls, boutiques and artists. Hi! I'm Kelly. I've enjoyed living in my 1920's West Asheville bungalow for 20 years. I'm a Kripalu Yoga Teacher and teach full-time from my home studio.

5 Things I Love:
Friendship and laughter
Swinging on my front porch
Tending to my home and gardens
Breathing, Stretching and Contemplation
Hiking in the woods with plenty of fresh air, sunshine and mountaintop vistas
Meaningful conversations
Good coffee, chocolate and cheese!

I am a part of all that I have met;
Yet all experience is an arch wheretho’
Gleams that untravell’d world whose margin fades
Forever and forever when I move. - Tennyson’s Ulysses

name: Upstream Bohemian - Ask about Wedding Venue
description: Melt away stress with the calming jets of the rooftop hot tub atop this modern architectural home. This eco-friendly residence features natural wood and stone finishes throughout, contrasting textures and patterns, and an outdoor dining space. neighborhood_overview: The home is close to everything Asheville has to offer. This house is directly across from the French Broad River, Carrier Park, bike paths, the green way and a boat ramp. There are also outdoor activities just next door at Climbmax.
host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

host_about:
My husband, Max and I moved to Asheville, NC, in 2001 and love living here! I was raised in San Miguel de Allende, Mexico, where my father taught photography and journalism at the Instituto Allende. I still have the home there in which I grew up!
I moved to Sausalito, California where I became a Strategy Implementation Consultant. As a bilingual and bicultural person, I was able to work  in 11 countries in Western Europe, South America, and North America. It was a great life, and I met wonderful people from all over the world.    I am also a song-writer and an author, and love music of all kinds from all parts of the world.
     Max was born in L.A., "grew up" in Berkeley, taught high school for many years and then went into the building trades for another lifetime. 
     In 2001, my husband and I moved to Asheville, NC, and we love it! Being in the mountains, in a glorious little town is perfect for us in our retirement phase of life, or our "repurposed" phase, as my husband likes to say.   
     We have two small dogs (a chihuahua mix and a mountain feist, both under 16 pounds). 
     We live on two acres, surrounded by wonderful, local neighbors that we are blessed to have around us.  
     We are foodies, love to cook and love to eat out, and can recommend lots of restaurants, though it's hard to keep up as a new and great one seems toped up every week here!
     We're easy going, like hosting friends, family and our AirBnB guests. Kelle was in the hotel and restaurant business decades ago, and this is a gentle step back into something she found much fun to pursue. 

Life is good, and we would  love to share it with you.

host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

host_about:
“Travel changes you. As you move through this life and this world you change things slightly, you leave marks behind, however small. And in return, life—and travel—leaves marks on you.”  – Anthony Bourdain.

We LIVE to travel! Heather spent many years working in the airline industry which allowed us to see 40+ countries. The Anthony Bourdain show “No Reservations”  sums up our travel style. We tend to book the first night to recover from jet lag and then keep the rest of the trip open. We like to see where our travels want to take us. Seeking out the “undiscovered” places and truly connecting with locals is what we are all about. Some of our favorites: Luang Prabang / Bagan / Zanzibar / Bali / Colombia / Ronda (got engaged) / Samana, Dominican Republic (got married) / Chicago / Isla Holbox (shhhh, keep it a secret). Through many of these travels Airbnb has been a big piece of the puzzle.  

The two of us met in Aspen, CO. Heather is originally from Chicago and Mark from Virginia Beach. Although Heather loved city life her wanderlust brought her to Aspen for thirteen years.  Mark had been living in Washington D.C. doing the daily grind as an architect and had heard about a firm in Aspen that was hiring. He jumped on the chance and never looked back!  Aspen was a fantastic place to live and truly enjoy life. It taught us that you can live more simply and have a healthier quality of life. 

After a long stint out west and with a child on the way we decided it was time to be closer to family. We had a list of 30 towns all over the midwest and eastern U.S. which we either visited or did research on. After visiting Asheville we knew it was our next stop in life. Mark has opened his own office and Heather teaches at a creative arts center while studying interior design. Besides continuing to travel, we hike with our son and two dogs as often as possible and love checking out the awesome breweries and restaurants Asheville has to offer. We've also just begun hosting on Airbnb and really enjoy meeting fellow travelers and hosting them in our guest suite. 

We hope to inspire others to get out of their comfort zone and check out other places and people on this amazing planet! 

"Not until we are lost do we begin to understand ourselves." 
- Henry David Thoreau

host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

Born in NC, attended UNC-Chapel Hill and got a degree in Journalism. My mom's side of the family has lived in Western North Carolina for the past century and a half. I have relatives buried in the Riverside Cemetery, which we can see from our backyard.
However, I lived most of my adult life on the West Coast. After college, I drove west in a school bus and eventually landed outside Eugene, OR, next to a creek, grew lots of my food, and had a sewing business, selling at the Saturday Market, Circle of Hands and craft fairs up and down the West Coast.
I have been to all 50 states, Canada, several Central American countries, Caribbean islands and Europe. I LOVE meeting people from all around the world and have studied conflict resolution in large groups of people using World Work. I am a therapist full time, offering massage therapy as well as Bodywisdom Therapy, helping people unravel the messages of their bodies, at a location on Merrimon Avenue. I speak a bit of French and Spanish, but am alas, no longer fluent.
My son and I moved back to WNC several years ago to be near my Mom, who lives in Yancey County. I know some sweet areas to visit around the area and are including them in a notebook in the rooms. 
I love being able to offer people a centrally located place to enjoy what WNC has to offer, as well as a prime walking neighborhood to have access to downtown Asheville hotspots. 
I turned both bedrooms and bathrooms downstairs into places that I would like to visit myself, using art from my own collection, and textures and colors that I love.
We have friends and family over on a regular basis so there is a bit of hustle and bustle at times. If you have children, or like to come and go and appreciate the outdoors, you will fit right in! If you want privacy, the private entrance and keypad will fit your needs. If you want total peace and quiet, I am afraid we won't be your cup of tea.
Living lightly on the earth is a core value for me so we recycle as much as possible, and keep our throwaway consumables to a minimum. 
Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

host_about:
I am a jewelry artist here in the River Arts District in Asheville, NC. I can assure you Asheville is a fantastic place to visit and you leave wanting more!  I lived out west for 20 years prior to moving here 6+ years ago.  I am amazed every day at the beauty of the Western North Carolina area, the southern hospitality, and the farm fresh food and craft beers and ciders!

   I love exploring the true character of an area and am always excited to find places to travel that have maintained their own unique character.  I definitely would say I've been off the beaten path just about everywhere I've traveled including Mongolia, Patagonia, Iceland and more!  My blessings are counted everyday knowing that I live in such a special place and it is such a pleasure to be able to offer a space that allows others to experience Asheville to the fullest as well.  
     My husband Brandon and I welcome you to our home just outside downtown Asheville.  The neighborhood is quiet and the location can’t be beat.  Please let us know if you need anything additional to make your stay more pleasant:)

neighborhood_overview:
☀☀☀ LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION! ☀☀☀
If you’ve ever wandered through downtown Asheville, then you’ve felt the wanderlust (and “wonder-lust)” of this historic warren.

Here, connecting two of the city’s most sought-after streets – W. Walnut and Woodfin/Hiawassee – Carolina Lane is a quiet (for the city) alley, long known to the real Asheville. This is where Oscar winning actress Frances McDormond conspicuously smoked her cigarettes after a day of filming in the area and industry once reigned. And this neighborhood? Well, it’s still a place where restaurants go unadvertised and the best bars have no signs, just a door. A place where high-end art galleries about record shops, upscale shoe stores, and more.

And, while Real Life may be about compromise – sacrifice This to get That – we believe that vacation should be a special time. A time you get both This and That, no compromise required.

33 Caroline Lane is your no-compromise-required desti
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

host_about:
I am a jewelry artist here in the River Arts District in Asheville, NC. I can assure you Asheville is a fantastic place to visit and you leave wanting more!  I lived out west for 20 years prior to moving here 6+ years ago.  I am amazed every day at the beauty of the Western North Carolina area, the southern hospitality, and the farm fresh food and craft beers and ciders!

   I love exploring the true character of an area and am always excited to find places to travel that have maintained their own unique character.  I definitely would say I've been off the beaten path just about everywhere I've traveled including Mongolia, Patagonia, Iceland and more!  My blessings are counted everyday knowing that I live in such a special place and it is such a pleasure to be able to offer a space that allows others to experience Asheville to the fullest as well.  
     My husband Brandon and I welcome you to our home just outside downtown Asheville.  The neighborhood is quiet and the location can’t be beat.  Please let us know if you need anything additional to make your stay more pleasant:)

I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering.  I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing.

If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

Hey - I'm Christine.

I moved to Asheville in the early 90's to escape Northern Virginia and my post-college cubicle job. I wanted to be a songwriter...which thrilled my parents to no end.

In 2010, as a result of requests from so many creative entrepreneurial types (and being burnt out from 250 days a year on the road), I started a business coaching company here in Asheville. That became an online training resource, and we've hosted clients from all over the world at our retreats and events here. These days, like so many of us, I spend more time on Zoom than anything else. :)

Hosting guests has been an unexpected joy and new passion for me.  I love being able to provide all the amenities and experiences for travelers and vacationers and work-from-homers... mostly based on 15 years of staying in every hotel (ahem, and motel) chain and city across the U.S.  I'm still learning so much.

I love all things nature. Trees, birds, bears, mountains, dirt. I strive to contribute the creative and natural spirit of this precious area, even as it grows at a crazy pace.

neighborhood_overview: The Cane Creek Valley is arguably one of the most beautiful areas in western NC. It is super convenient as a "base camp" from which to explore the many amenities the region has to offer, from the restaurants and shops of Asheville and Hendersonville, to the waterfalls of Brevard and trails off the Blue Ridge Parkway.  The 1.5 acre property where the apartment is located is level, open, and commands a view of Burney Mountain that changes with the seasons, the time of day,  and the weather. Rise early enough in the morning and you'll see the whisps of "smoke" and fog that give the Smoky Mountains their name. In the evening, experience the golden glow as the sun goes down, and enjoy a crackling fire from the comfort of Adirondack chairs.  It's easy, relaxed mountain living at its finest! The neighborhood is also fairly level and perfect for a walk or jog. Fletcher Park is just minutes away, with a great playground for children, trails for longer walks, runs, and safe bicycling.
host_about:
My husband Larry is a former TV news anchor and I was a Communications Director for our local school system before we became Realtors in western NC. We've lived here since 2005 and love life in the Smoky Mountains. We also love introducing the lifestyle, sights, and amenities here to our clients and to the guests who stay in our "Cane Creek Valley Swim-Soak-Stay" guest quarters.

We love to travel around the country and overseas every chance we get, so we know what travelers need and appreciate during a stay away from home.  

We have four adult children and four grandchildren spread out across the U.S., but our current "children" are our two beloved pups, Toby the Cairn Terrier and Greta the rescue pup, who form the "doggie welcoming committee."

We love meeting new people and exploring new places. We treat others the way we would like to be treated, and welcome strangers as friends.  We're non-smokers, and expect our guests to be, too. Most of all, we want our guests to have fun,  create great memories, and come back soon!

neighborhood_overview:
Kenilworth is a lovely, quiet neighborhood located in between Biltmore Avenue and Tunnel Road. You can walk down to Biltmore village in 10 minutes, south slope in 15 and downtown Asheville in 30. host_about:
Hey - I'm Christine.

I moved to Asheville in the early 90's to escape Northern Virginia and my post-college cubicle job. I wanted to be a songwriter...which thrilled my parents to no end.  

Turns out, Asheville was the perfect place to be creative, get quiet, wake the heck up - and spend the next 15 years as a touring performing songwriter on my own record label. (Shared stages with everyone from The Beach Boys to John Mayer to Nanci Griffith - and made 7 CD's along the way.)

In 2010, as a result of requests from so many creative entrepreneurial types (and being burnt out from 250 days a year on the road), I started a business coaching company here in Asheville. That became an online training resource, and we've hosted clients from all over the world at our retreats and events here. These days, like so many of us, I spend more time on Zoom than anything else. :)

Hosting guests has been an unexpected joy and new passion for me.  I love being able to provide all the amenities and experiences for travelers and vacationers and work-from-homers... mostly based on 15 years of staying in every hotel (ahem, and motel) chain and city across the U.S.  I'm still learning so much.

I love all things nature. Trees, birds, bears, mountains, dirt. I strive to contribute the creative and natural spirit of this precious area, even as it grows at a crazy pace.

host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

neighborhood_overview:
We are centrally located on the Greenway bike paths and 2 miles from the center of downtown. At most, we are a short Uber to all the local attractions.

For those who like to walk, the Asheville Adventure Center is right next door. Homegrown Restaurant and the Cascade Lounge are a short walk to the West.

12 Bones, the Wedge and the River Art Galleries are a short walk East. Following the bike path about a mile East lead to the amazing New Belgium Brewery Complex.
host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

host_about:
When I am in the mountains I am home!  I've lived in the Piedmont region of NC for 14 years now but, Asheville will always be home.  I am on the struggle bus of being a mom to my two boys, Kelvin 4 and Brody 2. My night in shining armor, Ben loves coaching middle school football and teaching 8th grade math. 
I was raised by a single mother from Cleveland Ohio with strong beliefs and the loudest laugh in the south! She believed that the most important things in life are those that can never be taken away; education and experiences!  She is the fundamental reason I am a realist, yet fearless and ready to take on the world. Our yearly trips to NYC led to us sharing a love of the city and Broadway! 
In 2007 Ben surprised me for a weekend trip to NYC. His first trip of many and my most memorable; he proposed on top of the Empire State Building! See why I call him my night in shining armor?!?  Of course Ben caught the travel bug too and has been back to NYC countless times! He's expanded to international travel! The Montford Area Historic District is one of the prettiest neighborhoods in the country--though we're admittedly a little biased. Most of the neighborhood's residences were constructed between 1890 and 1920 in the Victorian or Queen Anne Victorian styles, though you'll also find architecture in the Arts and Crafts, Neoclassical, and Colonial Revival styles. Residents pride themselves on their gardening and landscaping expertise, benefited in no small part by the region's capacity for growing an incredible diversity of flora, from the signature magnolia trees, to flowering shrubs like the rhododendron & azalea, to bamboo, succulents, and so much more.

The gorgeous local cemetery is worth a visit, marking the final resting place of authors Thomas Wolfe and O. Henry. North Montford was once home to the Highland Hospital, in which Zelda Fitzgerald tragically died in a fire in 1948.

description:
Welcome to the Sallie Lee Cottage! We hope you will enjoy your stay in Asheville in this charmingly renovated Historic Montford Cottage!
The Sallie Lee Cottage is amongst the oldest homes in Asheville and is believed to have been built around 1883. This amazing Cottage has been well preserved and restored to her former glory.
Located less than 1 mile from downtown Asheville!

The space
Proud to be a Victorian, the Sallie Lee Cottage is an exquisite example of the architectural wonders of the late 1800s. Around 1880, Sallie Lee built a stick-style Victorian cottage on Ashland Avenue. In doing this, she became the first woman to own a home in Western North Carolina. The cornerstone of this beautiful home centers around the exterior architectural displays of lines, angles, and ornate grids. Furthermore, the interior is equally exceptional, centering around its unique triangular fireplace; which results a distinct Latin cross floor plan.

The home

The cottage located in the Montford area and is within walking distance to downtown Asheville. This cottage is the recipient of both the Carraway Award of Merit from Preservation North Carolina and a Griffin Award from the Preservation Society of Asheville and Buncombe County.

Located in East Asheville in the 28805 zip code, Haw Creek was named for the native Black Haw shrub or small tree (Viburnum prunifolium) that grew more abundantly years ago along the moist soils of the valley, especially along Haw Creek itself.

Haw Creek valley’s southern boundary extends from US Highway 70/Tunnel Road at I-240 eastward along Tunnel Road to Maple Springs Road. Its west boundary is formed by Piney Mountain/Bear Mountain ridge; Town Mountain creates the northern boundary; and the Blue Ridge Parkway stretches along most of its eastern border.

Haw Creek was settled in the early 1800’s as a farming community with the first school established in 1842 on the site of the present day Bethesda Cemetery. Haw Creek has two main entrances with very narrow roads throughout the valley. host_about:
Emilie first fell in love with Asheville over 20 years ago when she attended Rockbrook Camp in the heart of a wooded mountain in Brevard, NC. Those mountains, so different from the beaches of her childhood, kept her coming back for ten years. There is something majestic about the Blue Ridge Mountains that blanket Western North Carolina, at over 1 billion years old, they are some of the oldest mountains in the entire world.

Arturo came to Asheville for the first time in 2012 and was quickly enamoured with the outdoor culture, so different from his 22 years in New York City, but so reminiscent of his childhood in the gentle hills of Puebla, Mexico. For him, it was a desire to start a family and a business and seek a better quality of life and he quickly found himself thirsty for everything that Asheville has to offer.

Emilie and Arturo met in 2008 while working together as sommeliers in the Lower East Side of Manhattan at The Ten Bells. Their working relationship was incredible, and over the next six years that relationship became a fine tuned machine- customers would always comment about the way they were able to seamlessly run the entire restaurant without even speaking. Learning the way one another worked over those first six years was the beginning of a true friendship that blossomed into love.

With 35 years of fine dining experience between the two, a Bed and Breakfast seemed like the perfect next adventure. Their penchant for hospitality and intuitive service and their true joy in meeting new people and making new friends put them in a unique position to choose their next path.

Emilie’s first Bed and Breakfast plan was written in the back of a college notebook when she was 18, wandering around Maine searching for the perfect wraparound porch. In 2011, she and Arturo decided to give those Bed and Breakfast dreams a trial run, and opened a small B&B in their East Village apartment. While tiny, it gave them a wonderful test-run on breakfast planning, scheduling, cleaning, decorating, recipe testing and conflict management. They loved it all!

The tri-lingual couple feel that they will bring a new, re-invented experience to the somewhat clichéd country B&B Inn. Asheville is no longer a sleepy town with boarded up buildings, it is a hub of restaurants, nightlife, music, beer and outdoor adventure. It’s not only the perfect place to call home, it is the perfect place to welcome someone into yours.

The house is situated near the end/top of the mountain, and the last section of the road near the house is packed gravel. The road can be narrow in spots, so please drive carefully to be mindful of other cars.

neighborhood_overview:
Just across the French Broad River from downtown, West Asheville (28806) is a mecca for originality. For the past few years, people have flocked to this funky neighborhood, either to visit or buy a quaint cottage within walking distance of the many new businesses that have opened in the area.

Haywood Road has been the main street of West Asheville for more than a century. Old buildings are now home to modern businesses, but the street still has a small hometown feel. As you walk down the street, you will see old buildings renovated for new businesses side-by-side with second- and third-generation shops. There are now many restaurants, breweries, pubs with frequent live music, bakeries, a variety of resale consignment shops, vintage clothing boutiques and even a half-dozen record shops lining the road that appeal to visitors interested in sampling the unique, bohemian flavor of Asheville.

The neighborhood offers great walking along nearby Reed Creek Greenway, in historic Riverside Cemetery, or on the neighborhood sidewalks.

For families with children, there are 3 parks within short walking distance including one at the end of the block. A trio of grocery stores (Trader Joe's, Whole Foods, and Harris Teeter) is a few blocks east.

Asheville offers great restaurants, a vibrant arts scene, historic architecture, and lush rolling mountains with great hiking.

The Biltmore House, the Blue Ridge Parkway, the River Arts District, tons of breweries, and everything else Asheville offers are a short drive away.

Breweries, restaurants, and coffee shops are overflowing from the nearby RAD. Our neighbors are lively and friendly, and you’re likely to get a small-town wave. These are good people. Please respect our neighbors by driving slow.
host_about:
I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering. The mountains called my name, and my would-be manager also called my name (to offer me a job),  so I set out on the 17hr drive and only looked back once...because I thought I saw a bear.

 I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. 

If there's an opportunity to go fishing, I usually take the bait. I own a small fleet of fishing kayaks and like to take day trips out on the local waters to pursue bass, trout and gorgeous scenery. If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

description:

neighborhood_overview:
Riceville is the least developed quadrant of the immediate Asheville area. The Blue Ridge Parkway access is about four miles away, but it is actually much closer, just up on the side of High Swan.

Near the Brown House (about 300 yards away) is a home construction site that may generate noise during the work week, but it is quiet in the evening and on weekends. On the other side of our property is a Work Exchange Community whereby people live on the land and work on it in exchange for their dwelling space. Sometimes they play acoustic drums.

The traffic on the state road approaching our place is light, and local residents walk along it for exercise. On your drive in, you will likely see cows and wild turkeys. Over the ridge at the end of Shope Creek Road is National Forest access where you can hike and mountain bike. A few miles, 3 or so, to the east is Warren Wilson College.

Our property generally has a dark sky at night and is not a bad place
host_about:
Mick & Edie:

Mick loves to write stories and explore the world.  Edie loves to teach children and call folk dancing.  They both love to hike and visit with their grandchildren.  Their profile photo was taken at the North Carolina Arboretum, a place you must visit.  It's just off the Blue Ridge Parkway near the French Broad River.  Mick wrote and published an illustrated/photographic guide book to the Monarch butterfly migration over the southern Blue Ridge Parkway that you sometimes can find in Parkway bookstores.  The property has a milkweed garden just below the blueberry patch. Milkweed is the only plant that larval  Monarchs will eat. Edie is a musician who plays seasonally at the Biltmore Estate.
